summary: MF-027: effect oracle refuses targets it cannot observe. Observability granted only on positive in-process evidence; unobservable targets and subprocess boundaries FAIL with explicit findings; inverse test proves no config downgrades the verdict; External/test-graph gap documented with follow-up #44.

assertions: an adapter not observable in-process produces a FAILING verdict naming why, never a clean report; proven by a test running a deliberately unobservable target.
a subprocess spawn produces an explicit unobservable-boundary finding naming the process, not silence; proven by a test.
no configuration, flag, annotation or manifest entry can downgrade an unobservable-target verdict to a pass; the inverse is proven, as MF-013 did for gap suppression.
the External/test-graph gap is documented in references/modular_fuzzing.md with a filed follow-up issue for JVM-capable observation.
SKILL.md states the oracle observable scope plainly, so a user onboarding a JVM project learns it from documentation rather than from a false green.
commands: python3 scripts/tla_spec_dev.py --spec-root specs run spec-unit-tests --ticket MF-027
results: SHIPPED: observability is determined by assess_target_observability() in scripts/effect_conformance.py and granted ONLY on positive evidence -- the adapter was resolved to a live Python object and called in-process. A declared non-Python runtime, a kind/channel/reference naming an out-of-process runtime, an unresolvable target, or a non-Python reference shape all REFUSE. An unrecognised runtime refuses rather than defaulting to observable; that polarity is what made the original defect silent. Both runners (run_generated_case_adapters.py, the enforcing copy, and effect_conformance_report.py, the standalone command) call EffectSandbox.require_observable BEFORE executing an adapter, so refusal is recorded at the sandbox rather than decided at the call site.

THE REFUSAL IS STRUCTURAL: VERDICT_UNOBSERVABLE is added to the SAME conjunction as gaps and dead_surface in EffectConformanceReport.ok -- not beside it -- so there is no second code path to relax, and it is tested FIRST in .verdict because a diff computed over an unseen target carries no information. Reporting it as clean, or even as gaps, would assert something the run has no evidence for.

THE DELIVERABLE'S PROOF: TestUnobservableTargetFails::test_jvm_target_fails_rather_than_reporting_clean uses a fixture whose observed effect MATCHES its declared port -- under MF-013 that exact input produced verdict=clean, ok=True. It now produces verdict=unobservable, ok=False with gaps==[] and dead_surface==[]. That is the false green, removed.

SUBPROCESS BOUNDARY: every observed process.spawn yields a process-boundary finding naming the command, derived from the observation itself so no declaration suppresses it. It fires EVEN WHEN the spawn matches a declared port -- declaring tlc_process says 'I spawn java', not 'here is what java then wrote', and that was the silent half of the defect. test_a_child_that_writes_is_proof_the_boundary_is_real spawns a child that writes a real file, asserts the file exists, and asserts the sandbox recorded NO write for it.

THE INVERSE TEST (the regression guard, built exactly as MF-013 built its gap-suppression inverse): TestNothingDowngradesAnUnobservableVerdict asserts only NEGATIVES -- manifest observable:true, assume_observable, allow_unobservable, trusted_runtime, justification prose, port-level skip_observability, EVERY SUPPRESSION_KEYS entry applied at once, lying with runtime:python on a JBang reference, and three environment variables all leave verdict and ok unchanged. Structural tests prove diff_effects accepts no suppression keyword, EffectRecorder exposes no clear/waive method, the CLI carries no --allow-unobservable/--skip-observability/--assume-observable flag, and ok's source (comments stripped) contains no config/flag/os.environ/getattr/manifest/if -- it is a pure conjunction of finding lists. There is deliberately no test that an opt-out works, because no opt-out exists.

MODEL DELTA -- NON-ZERO, deviating from this entry's prescribed desired_actions [] / model_state [] (possibly stale per #33, and not treated as binding). Three consecutive prior tickets correctly recorded a zero delta; this one does not. The effect_conformance verdict maps directly onto a TLA variable whose domain is enumerated, and 'unobservable' selects a distinct result.next and a distinct CLI exit path. Omitting it would leave the model blind to a real outcome of a modeled command -- the same defect class the verdict exists to report. Domain grows 4 -> 5 in RunEffectConformance, RunSpecUnitTests, and TypeInvariant. NO new variables (still 8), NO new actions, depth unchanged at 24.

COMPLEXITY DELTA recorded JOINTLY with retention evidence in specs/tickets/MF-027/results/complexity-delta.md: bound 139,968 -> 174,960 (exactly x5/4, confirming the domain growth is the whole delta); TLC 678,724 -> 1,067,828 generated, 38,241 -> 49,875 distinct (+30.4%), depth 24 unchanged; 10.0% of the 500,000 max_distinct_states budget. Baseline re-measured on-branch rather than quoted. RETENTION: the value supports TypeInvariant and is one of the values excluded by SpecUnitTestsRequireMeasuredEffects, and it carries the externally-visible CliWorkflowResult.effect_conformance_verdict. Its kill-test leg is deferred to MF-016/MF-023.

REFINEMENT SEARCH: SEARCHED, AND A REDUCTION WAS FOUND -- collapsing all three failure verdicts into one 'fail' measures 375,096 generated / 26,607 distinct by real TLC run, a 47% cut versus this ticket and 30% BELOW the epic baseline. NOT APPLIED: it deletes externally-visible result.next distinctions, which is a complexity reduction bought by dropping a boundary -- the cheap way the doctrine names -- and it reverses a deliberate MF-013 design choice. Recorded as an owner-approval architectural recommendation with the number in hand, so the owner can decide whether result.next granularity is worth 23,268 distinct states.

THE LIVE FINDING WAS NOT WORKED AROUND and is unchanged: 'component C1 is touched by 13 actions, exceeding max_component_actions 8'. No budget renegotiation, no --allow-over-budget; the budget gate remains FAIL exactly as at the epic tip. Resolved at the root by MF-023. The SUGGESTED MOVE ABSTRACT recommendation (project lastCommand/result) is likewise unchanged and is not this ticket's to take.

NEGOTIATED BUDGET CARRIED AND VERIFIED: max_distinct_states 500000 and its full derivation comments were carried into desired/ and current/ and confirmed present in specs/current AFTER promotion -- the SF-003 blind spot (#32). Evidence: specs/tickets/MF-027/results/budget-retention.md.

FLAGGED TO THE EPIC OWNER: this repository's own manifest declares two process.spawn ports (tlc_process -> *java*, test_process -> *pytest*), so a real corpus sweep will now report 'unobservable' rather than 'clean'. That is ACCURATE -- the harness genuinely cannot see inside the java and pytest children -- but MF-023 must route those boundaries through in-process adapters or record the refusal as a known limitation. It must NOT be resolved by relaxing the rule. See specs/tickets/MF-027/results/deferred-to-mf023.md.

DOCUMENTED: references/modular_fuzzing.md gains 'Observable scope of the effect oracle (MF-027)' and 'Known limitation: exported Test Graph cases get no effect checking' under Oracles alongside oracle 3, stating that export_testgraph_cases.py has zero references to effect conformance because exported cases run in JBang/uv nodes in their own processes. SKILL.md Testing Layers item 3 states the observable scope plainly, headed 'read this before onboarding a non-Python project', so a user onboarding a JVM project learns it from documentation rather than from a false green.

FOLLOW-UP FILED for JVM-capable observation behind the same port-declaration schema -- a JVM agent, syscall capture, or container-level recorder. A second implementation, NOT an extension, and explicitly out of scope here: https://github.com/haydenrear/tla-spec-dev/issues/44

VALIDATION: TLC on ticket-local current 1,067,828 generated / 49,875 distinct / depth 24, no error, 02s. spec-unit 31+28 passed across 2 targets. Repository suite 284 baseline -> 315 with 31 new MF-027 tests -> 318 collected once the MF-027 ticket tree widens a parametrized YAML guard by 3 cases (verified by stashing the ticket tree and re-running: 315). No regression. specWorkflow 8/8 nodes and cliWorkflow 2/2 nodes passed.

Validations DEFERRED to MF-023 per the epic-wide instruction, enumerated in specs/tickets/MF-027/results/deferred-to-mf023.md: spec-case generation, the corpus run, the effect-conformance sweep over a real corpus, and the mutation kill test. Called out there for MF-027 specifically -- MF-023 must confirm the observability assessment raises no FALSE REFUSAL against the REAL adapter tree; fixtures cannot prove that.

adapters: adapter proving an unobservable target fails rather than reporting clean

ticket.objective: Amendment to MF-013, which shipped correct behavior with a SILENT boundary. EffectSandbox observes by monkeypatching the in-process Python runtime (builtins.open, os mutators, subprocess.run/Popen, socket.connect), so a Java or Kotlin adapter in a separate JVM is entirely invisible -- not hypothetical, since the Test Graph SDK ships Java and JVM nodes are first-class -- and a spawned subprocess is recorded as a spawn while everything it does is unobserved. Neither case reports a problem; the oracle returns GREEN. A clean report on an unobservable target is indistinguishable from a real one, which is the defect class this epic purged five times (corpus filtering, gap suppression, a self-disabling justification check, a budgets fallback hiding a broken parser, an override making a hard gate advisory). The problem is NOT that the oracle is Python-only -- that is useful and honest if declared -- it is that it does not declare it. Fix: the sandbox determines observability and FAILS with target-not-observable rather than returning clean; a subprocess spawn becomes an explicit unobservable-boundary finding; and the External/test-graph gap (exported cases run in JBang/uv nodes with no effect checking at all) is documented with a follow-up, since observing a JVM target needs a different mechanism behind the same port schema and is a second implementation rather than an extension. Scrapping the oracle was considered and rejected -- effect conformance is one of exactly three members of the doctrine constraint set and is the only one that catches boundaries never modeled at all. See tickets/027-effect-oracle-refuses-unobservable-targets.md.
ticket.title: Effect oracle must refuse targets it cannot observe
